Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

help! interjection

a cry for help

also somebody help!, help me!, help us!

classical

Plaut. Men. 1000: Epidamniēnsēs, subvenīte, cīvēs.

Subvenīte!

imperative of subveniō, with the dative of the one helped; singular subvenī · Wiktionary

help! (to several)

“Come to the rescue!”: the plainest cry.

Other words

  • Vestram fidem! — help, good people! (I appeal to your protection)

    accusative, with obsecrō or implōrō understood or expressed; vostram in Plautus · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 615: vostram ego implōrō fidem; Plaut. Men. 999: opsecrō vestram fidem

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    With prō, prō fidem! (Plaut. Amph. 376). The gods’ version, prō deum atque hominum fidem!, is mostly an outburst of indignation (see good heavens!).

Examples

  • quō rapitis mē? quō fertis mē? periī, opsecrō vestram fidem, Epidamniēnsēs, subvenīte, cīvēs.

    Where are you dragging me? where are you carrying me? I’m done for! I beg your help, people of Epidamnus: help, citizens!Plaut. Men. 999–1000

  • Prō Cȳrēnēnsēs populārēs, vostram ego implōrō fidem

    O people of Cyrene, I implore your helpPlaut. Rud. 615

  • prō fidem, Thēbānī cīvēs.

    Help, citizens of Thebes!Plaut. Amph. 376

See also help, I’ll help you, good heavens!.
